subject: Pricing touchpoint — confirm economic buyer & cost scenarios
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brightlane.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 15:08:00 -0400
Subject: Pricing touchpoint — confirm economic buyer & cost scenarios

Liam — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we can get a clean pricing packet to procurement: 

Summary of the ask
- You want a simple, comparable cost model for Chat+Embedding usage across three monthly volumes (10M / 50M / 200M tokens) so finance can evaluate runway and ROI.
- We discussed options: Hosted API (pay-as-you-go) vs Reserved/Dedicated capacity (commitment discounts + lower unit cost).

Immediate asks for Brightlane
1) Please confirm who will be the economic buyer / finance approver for this project so we can route the contract and procurement materials.
2) Confirm the budget owner / cost center (e.g., Product Ops, Analytics) and the expected procurement timeline (procurement window, target sign date).

Initial assumptions I used for the attached scenarios (we'll refine once you confirm buyer and commitment term):
- Hosted baseline unit: $1,200 per 1M tokens
- Reserved/Dedicated (6–12 month commit): ~ $800 per 1M tokens (rough)
- Token mix assumption: 80% chat/generation tokens, 20% embeddings (embeddings slightly cheaper in practice but folded into the unit economics here for simplicity)

Attached: pricing-scenarios.xlsx — simple tiers/line items for 10M / 50M / 200M monthly volumes and a 6-month committed scenario.

If you can confirm the economic buyer and budget owner today, Marissa will produce a one-page procurement summary and Neha can outline preferred commercial terms (FF, net-45, etc.).

Thanks,
Sean
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0198

[Attachment: pricing-scenarios.xlsx]

Thanks Sean — useful recap. Quick answers from our side:
- Economic buyer / finance approver: Anna Bradley (CFO) — cc'ing below.
- Budget owner / cost center: Product Ops — lead is Carlos Mendez (we'll loop him if you want to include product-side stakeholders).
- Procurement timeline: target decision within 4–6 weeks; small pilot could be contracted faster.

Can you include for each volume (10M / 50M / 200M):
- Estimated monthly cost (Hosted vs Reserved)
- Effective $ per 1M tokens (so our finance team sees unit economics)
- A short note on how unit price changes with a 6-month vs 12-month commit

Anna — we chatted about the use case (customer responses + recommendations). If you are the right person to weigh in on budget, can you confirm and I'll push this through procurement?

Cheers,
Liam

Hi Liam / Anna — looping in the scenarios Sean mentioned. I put together the attached spreadsheet and pasted the quick summary below so finance has a one-glance view.

Snapshot (assumptions: Hosted = $1,200 / 1M; Reserved = $800 / 1M; reserved assumes 6–12 month commitment):

Volume: 10M tokens/month
- Hosted: 10 x $1,200 = $12,000 / month
- Reserved (6mo commit): 10 x $800 = $8,000 / month
- Effective $/1M tokens: Hosted = $1,200; Reserved = $800

Volume: 50M tokens/month
- Hosted: 50 x $1,200 = $60,000 / month
- Reserved (6mo commit): 50 x $800 = $40,000 / month
- Effective $/1M tokens: Hosted = $1,200; Reserved = $800

Volume: 200M tokens/month
- Hosted: 200 x $1,200 = $240,000 / month
- Reserved (12mo commit + volume tiering): ~ $650–750 / 1M -> ~$130,000–$150,000 / month

Notes and recommendations:
- For pilots (<=50M), hosted is simplest; if you expect sustained growth to >100M, reserved capacity or a blended committed model reduces unit cost materially.
- We can structure a stepped ramp (3 months pilot hosted, then convert to 6mo reserved at agreed commit) to lower initial friction for procurement.
- We will provide a one-page procurement summary (SOW, SLAs, SOC2 evidence link) once you confirm the approver.

Attaching pricing-scenarios.xlsx with line-item CSV and a 6-month vs 12-month comparison.

Best,
Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

- Preliminary budget range for FY26 (for this initiative): $60,000 — $180,000 / year depending on scope. That implies we would prefer a conservative 6-month committed pilot first (to validate ROI) with an option to extend to 12 months at a negotiated unit price.
- Please include a 6-month committed scenario in the packet with monthly amounts and an expected uplift if we convert to 12 months.
- Procurement team needs a 1-page summary (cost, term, SLAs) and a filled procurement form. We'll aim to route internally within 2 weeks after we receive that.
